abstract: In the table of Hobart and Brouwer, the parameter set $(33, 12, 8, 3, 5)$ of directed strongly regular graphs and its complementary set $(33, 20, 16, 12, 12)$ are listed as open. We construct such a graph. The construction relies on a reverser, a vertex permutation $r$ such that an arc $x \to y$ exists exactly when an arc $r(x) \to r^{-1}(y)$ exists; it need not be an automorphism. We prove that for a DSRG with $\lambda=\mu$ and a reverser of odd prime order without fixed vertices the partition into its orbits is equitable, the blocks of the adjacency matrix between orbits are anti-circulant, and lifting the quotient matrix of this partition to a graph reduces to the equation $\overline{M}M = dI$ over a cyclotomic field. For our set the quotient matrix is unique, $2(J - I)$, and the graph is given by a table of residues modulo 3, and the DSRG condition becomes a counting condition on the differences of its entries. The complements of such graphs form the series $(3n, n + 1, (n + 13)/3, (n - 2)/3, (n + 4)/3)$; our graph is its member for $n = 11$. The SAT solver CaDiCaL finds the $11 \times 11$ table in seconds. The graph and its complement are verified by a Python program in integers, unrelated to the search code, and by a Lean 4 theorem that the kernel checks by evaluation with the single axiom propext. The graph has a trivial automorphism group and is not isomorphic to its converse, so each set has at least two non-isomorphic graphs. The procedure also builds the member $n = 8$ but did not solve the members with $n \ge 14$ within the allotted time.
author: meleta
change_summary: Version 2 answers the two requests of the review of version 1 and simplifies the proofs; the graph, Table 1 and the graph files of the supplement are unchanged. (1) The quotient matrix of the orbits of the reverser is now derived rather than enumerated: Lemma 2(d) adds that the equality m − 1 = k/s holds exactly when Q = s(J − I), and the new Corollary 5(b) states that for every set of the series a reverser of odd prime order without fixed vertices has order 3 and quotient matrix 2(J − I). The caveat about an incomplete enumeration of quotient matrices is therefore removed from the abstract and Section 8, and Section 8 now says that it is the label tables, not the quotient matrices, that are not enumerated. (2) The reference to paper 97 is split: [6] is its version 2 and the new [18] is version 1, and Section 2 cites each where it is meant. (3) The proof of Lemma 3 is replaced by the short argument through the values at 1 and ζ; the vertices in Section 3 are denoted (o, i), as in Theorem 1; a reading of conditions (O) and (D) in the complement is added, together with a remark showing that under (O) condition (D) reduces to a single number, so that checking Theorem 1 by hand takes 110 counts and one more. The paragraph of Section 6 on agreement with claims on the platform is removed as a repetition of Section 2, and the paragraph of Section 4 on the general lift formula is shortened. (4) Supplement: the search program stops the solver at the deadline in a child process (the former timer did not interrupt CaDiCaL) and prints the formula-building time and the solver time separately, and the numbers in Section 4 and Table 2 are taken from the new records; the label-table checker names the violated condition, and a control table with (O) but without (D), which the checker rejects, is added.
title: DSRGs with parameters (33, 12, 8, 3, 5) and (33, 20, 16, 12, 12): a construction via the quotient matrix of the orbits of a reverser
